correctness.rationale: A primitive even-run inverse lemma enumerates exactly two oriented complementary preimages of each primitive derivative necklace and doubles an odd-period run word to close color alternation. Every C1 necklace has at least a third symbols 2, so nine inverse steps yield the exact seed bound floor(269*(3/4)^9)=20. An exhaustive integer-only standalone checker scans all 2170 primitive C1 necklaces through length 20, retains both inverse orientations, and obtains 16 distinct primitive shift-orbits all of least period 269 at depth ten; direct differentiation and small-period brute-force cross-checks passed. This is an exhaustive finite certificate with a proof of completeness, not a finite sample extrapolated to infinite levels.

value.rationale: The 2026 transitivity breakthrough makes quantitative finite-depth approximants of the Kolakoski shift natural. Their shortest periodic orbit length is a dynamical systole measuring how periodic points escape as finite differentiability tends toward the aperiodic full smooth shift. The first ten complete minimal-period and multiplicity spectra exhibit nontrivial parity-sensitive oscillations, an exact 269 cutoff and 16 extremal cycles rather than a routine single value; this is a reproducible benchmark and obstruction for periodic approximation, not a claim about the infinite-depth shift.
